page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.12xlarge is an arm64-based compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS Graviton architecture. The configuration supplies 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding multithreading contention. System memory totals 96.0 GB, providing a standard compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB per physical core.

The instance includes 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-throughput and low-latency ephemeral disk space directly attached to the host. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The platform does not incorporate dedicated GPU acceleration and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The architectural balance prioritizes integer compute throughput and direct local disk input/output over high RAM density. While the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU profile limits workloads requiring massive in-memory databases, it delivers consistent execution speed for parallelized processing. Recommended applications include distributed batch compute clusters, continuous integration build jobs, media encoding, and data transformation pipelines that require fast local scratch disks.

The instance features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs clocked at 3.3 GHz, offering single-threaded core isolation with 96.0 GB of system memory, matching a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Designed for IO-intensive computational jobs, it includes 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no GPU accelerators. The hardware configuration emphasizes dense multi-core compute combined with rapid local storage access, though the 1:2 memory-to-core ratio restricts deployments requiring large in-memory working sets. The instance is suited for batch processing, software compilation, distributed analytics, and compute-bound tasks requiring substantial local scratch space.
